title: 2024 final paper (In20)
intro:
**2 hours · 100 marks · 4 questions of 25 marks · answer all.** Closed book; an approved calculator only. Derivations are needed only where asked.

Work on paper. When you submit (or time runs out) every part shows a **worked answer** and a **mark scheme** - tick the points your answer contains to get your score.

The questions are as set in the 2024 paper, with worked answers added. Original: [EN3330 2024 paper (PDF)](/notes-files/cse/sem7/en3330-paper-2024.pdf). Where the printed question has a typo, the answer says which reading it uses.

sections.title: Answer ALL questions
sections.blurb: Four questions, 25 marks each. Calculator allowed; closed book.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Five critical points of a function $f(x)$, $\{x \in \mathbb{R} : -1.5 \le x \le 13\}$, are shown in Figure Q1.1. State the given critical points A, B, C, D and E.

![Figure Q1.1: critical points of f(x)](/notes-files/cse/sem7/en3330-2024-fig-q1.png)
parts.answer:
| Point | x (approx.) | Type |
|---|---|---|
| A | 0 | **Saddle / stationary inflection** - $f' = 0$ but $f$ keeps increasing on both sides: neither max nor min |
| B | 2 | **Local maximum** - and the **global maximum** on $[-1.5, 13]$ (f ≈ 3.2 is higher than both end values, ≈ −7.8 and ≈ −1.5) |
| C | 5.7 | **Global minimum** (f ≈ −16, the lowest value in the interval) |
| D | 9.3 | **Local maximum** (f ≈ −0.5, below B) |
| E | 11.7 | **Local minimum** (f ≈ −4.8, above C) |

Check the end points when you say "global": on a closed interval the global extremes can sit at an end point that is not a critical point.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Consider
$$\min_{\mathbf{x}}\ f(\mathbf{x}) = \Big(x_1 - \tfrac43\Big)^n + (x_2 - 5)^n \quad\text{s.t.}\quad x_1 + 2x_2 - 8 \ge 0,\ 2x_1 + x_2 - 6 \le 0,\ -x_1 \le 0,\ -x_2 \le 0.$$
(i) Sketch the feasible region. **[4]** (ii) For $n = 2$ sketch the minimum of $f$ and the feasible region on one diagram. **[6]** (iii) List the active and inactive constraints at that minimum. **[2]**
parts.answer:
**(i)** Boundary lines: $x_1 + 2x_2 = 8$ through (0, 4) and (8, 0) - feasible **above** it; $2x_1 + x_2 = 6$ through (0, 6) and (3, 0) - feasible **below** it; and $x_1 \ge 0$. They meet where $x_1 + 2x_2 = 8$ and $2x_1 + x_2 = 6$: $x_1 = 4/3$, $x_2 = 10/3$. The feasible region is the **triangle with vertices (0, 4), (0, 6) and (4/3, 10/3)** ($x_2 \ge 0$ is automatically satisfied).

**(ii)** For $n = 2$ the level sets are circles centred at $(4/3, 5)$. That centre is **infeasible**: $2(4/3) + 5 = 7.67 > 6$. So the constrained minimum is the point of the triangle closest to $(4/3, 5)$ - its projection onto the line $2x_1 + x_2 = 6$:
$$\mathbf{x}^* = \begin{bmatrix}4/3\\5\end{bmatrix} - \frac{2(4/3) + 5 - 6}{2^2 + 1^2}\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}4/3\\5\end{bmatrix} - \frac13\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}2/3\\14/3\end{bmatrix}.$$
It lies on the edge between (0, 6) and (4/3, 10/3) ($x_1 + 2x_2 = 10 \ge 8$ ✓), so $\mathbf{x}^* = (2/3, 14/3)$ with $f^* = (2/3)^2 + (1/3)^2 = 5/9$. The smallest circle touching the triangle is tangent to that edge.

![Feasible triangle, level circles and the constrained minimum](/notes-files/cse/sem7/en3330-2024-ans-q1b.png)

**(iii)** Active: $2x_1 + x_2 - 6 \le 0$ (holds with equality). Inactive: $x_1 + 2x_2 - 8 \ge 0$ (value 2 > 0), $-x_1 \le 0$, $-x_2 \le 0$.

points.text: Correct boundary lines and side of each
Diagram: circles tangent to the edge at x*

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: State the first-order (FONC) and second-order (SONC) necessary conditions for a local minimum of a multivariable function.
parts.answer:
At a local minimizer $\mathbf{x}^*$ of a twice-differentiable $f$ (interior point):
- **FONC:** $\nabla f(\mathbf{x}^*) = \mathbf{0}$.
- **SONC:** $\nabla^2 f(\mathbf{x}^*) \succeq 0$ - the Hessian is positive semidefinite.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For $f(\mathbf{x}) = \dfrac{x_1^3}{3} - \dfrac{9x_1^2}{2} + 20x_1 + x_2^2 - 6x_2 + 9$, identify the critical points and classify them.
parts.answer:
$\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x_1} = x_1^2 - 9x_1 + 20 = (x_1 - 4)(x_1 - 5) = 0 \Rightarrow x_1 = 4, 5$; $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x_2} = 2x_2 - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow x_2 = 3$.

Critical points: **(4, 3)** and **(5, 3)**. Hessian $\nabla^2 f = \begin{bmatrix}2x_1 - 9 & 0\\ 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}$.

- (4, 3): eigenvalues −1 and 2 - **indefinite → saddle point** (neither), $f = 29.33$.
- (5, 3): eigenvalues 1 and 2 - **positive definite → strict local minimum**, $f = 29.17$. (Not global: the cubic term makes $f \to -\infty$ as $x_1 \to -\infty$.)

questions.explain: Q1(b)(ii): the quickest route is "the minimum of a squared distance over a convex set is the projection of the centre onto the set" - then check which edge the projection lands on.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Consider $\min \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{d}\|_2^2$ s.t. $\mathbf{a}^T\mathbf{x} = b$, with $\mathbf{d}, \mathbf{a} \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $b \in \mathbb{R}$.
(i) Show it is equivalent to $\min\|\mathbf{y}\|_2^2$ s.t. $\mathbf{a}^T\mathbf{y} = c$, where $c = b - \mathbf{a}^T\mathbf{d}$. **[2]**
(ii) Use purely geometric arguments to find the optimal $\mathbf{x}^*$. **[5]**
parts.answer:
**(i)** Substitute $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{d}$ (a one-to-one shift). The objective becomes $\|\mathbf{y}\|_2^2$ and the constraint $\mathbf{a}^T(\mathbf{y} + \mathbf{d}) = b \iff \mathbf{a}^T\mathbf{y} = b - \mathbf{a}^T\mathbf{d} = c$. Same optimal value; $\mathbf{x}^* = \mathbf{y}^* + \mathbf{d}$.

**(ii)** $\{\mathbf{y} : \mathbf{a}^T\mathbf{y} = c\}$ is a **hyperplane** with normal $\mathbf{a}$. The point of a hyperplane closest to the origin is the foot of the perpendicular from the origin, so $\mathbf{y}^*$ is parallel to $\mathbf{a}$: $\mathbf{y}^* = t\mathbf{a}$. Putting it on the plane: $t\,\mathbf{a}^T\mathbf{a} = c \Rightarrow t = c/\|\mathbf{a}\|^2$. (Any other point $\mathbf{y}^* + \mathbf{v}$ with $\mathbf{a}^T\mathbf{v} = 0$ has $\|\mathbf{y}^* + \mathbf{v}\|^2 = \|\mathbf{y}^*\|^2 + \|\mathbf{v}\|^2$ by Pythagoras - larger.)
$$\mathbf{x}^* = \mathbf{d} + \frac{b - \mathbf{a}^T\mathbf{d}}{\|\mathbf{a}\|_2^2}\,\mathbf{a},$$
the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{d}$ onto the hyperplane.

points.text: Substitution y = x − d and transformed constraint

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: An energy-minimisation problem is $\min_{\mathbf{z}} \sum_{k=1}^m \beta_k\|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{b}_k\|_2^2$ with $\beta_k > 0$, $\mathbf{b}_k \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Using $\|\mathbf{z} - \mathbf{b}_k\|_2^2 = \mathbf{z}^T\mathbf{z} - 2\mathbf{z}^T\mathbf{b}_k + \mathbf{b}_k^T\mathbf{b}_k$, show that $\mathbf{z}^* = \dfrac{\sum_k \beta_k\mathbf{b}_k}{\sum_k\beta_k}$.
parts.answer:
Expand:
$$F(\mathbf{z}) = \sum_k\beta_k(\mathbf{z}^T\mathbf{z} - 2\mathbf{z}^T\mathbf{b}_k + \mathbf{b}_k^T\mathbf{b}_k) = \Big(\sum_k\beta_k\Big)\mathbf{z}^T\mathbf{z} - 2\mathbf{z}^T\Big(\sum_k\beta_k\mathbf{b}_k\Big) + \sum_k\beta_k\|\mathbf{b}_k\|^2.$$
Gradient (using $\nabla(\mathbf{z}^T\mathbf{z}) = 2\mathbf{z}$, $\nabla(\mathbf{z}^T\mathbf{c}) = \mathbf{c}$):
$$\nabla F = 2\Big(\sum_k\beta_k\Big)\mathbf{z} - 2\sum_k\beta_k\mathbf{b}_k = \mathbf{0} \;\Rightarrow\; \mathbf{z}^* = \frac{\sum_k\beta_k\mathbf{b}_k}{\sum_k\beta_k}.$$
Hessian $\nabla^2F = 2\big(\sum_k\beta_k\big)I \succ 0$ since every $\beta_k > 0$: $F$ is strictly convex, so this stationary point is the **unique global minimum** - the weighted centroid of the $\mathbf{b}_k$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: If $\mathbf{b}_1, \dots, \mathbf{b}_m$ ($m \le n$) are orthonormal, solve $\max_{\boldsymbol\beta}\ \sum_k\beta_k\|\mathbf{z}^* - \mathbf{b}_k\|_2^2$ s.t. $\sum_k\beta_k = 1$, $\beta_k > 0$.
parts.answer:
With $\sum\beta_k = 1$, $\mathbf{z}^* = \sum_k\beta_k\mathbf{b}_k$. Orthonormality gives $\|\mathbf{z}^*\|^2 = \sum_k\beta_k^2$, $\mathbf{z}^{*T}\mathbf{b}_k = \beta_k$, $\|\mathbf{b}_k\|^2 = 1$. So
$$\sum_k\beta_k\|\mathbf{z}^* - \mathbf{b}_k\|^2 = \sum_k\beta_k\Big(\sum_j\beta_j^2 - 2\beta_k + 1\Big) = \sum_j\beta_j^2 - 2\sum_k\beta_k^2 + 1 = 1 - \sum_k\beta_k^2.$$
Maximising $1 - \sum\beta_k^2$ means minimising $\sum\beta_k^2$ subject to $\sum\beta_k = 1$. Lagrangian $\sum\beta_k^2 - \nu(\sum\beta_k - 1)$: $2\beta_k = \nu$ for all $k$, so all equal: $\beta_k^* = 1/m$ (positive ✓). Optimal value $1 - 1/m$.

questions.explain: For (b), always finish with the Hessian - "stationary point" is not "minimum" until you have shown convexity.

questions.prompt:
Question 3. A PCB company makes types A, B and C ($x_A, x_B, x_C$ units) with profit $P = (60x_A + 20x_B(x_B - 10) + 10x_C) \times 10^3$.
- One labour hour makes one type A **or** one type B PCB; a type C needs two labour hours. 120 labour hours are allocated and **all** must be used.
- A type B needs 5 minutes of machine time; A needs twice that and C three times. 950 machine units are available and **all** must be used.
- Type A costs Rs 30 000; B costs half of A; C costs one third of B. The budget is Rs 2.5 × 10⁶.

parts.label: i
parts.prompt: Formulate the optimisation problem. All three types must be manufactured.
parts.answer:
Variables $x_A, x_B, x_C$. Costs: A 30 000, B 15 000, C 5 000 Rs. Machine time per unit: A 10, B 5, C 15 minutes.

*Assumption:* the 950 machine "hours" must be **minutes** - with at most 120 labour hours of production the machines can never use 950 hours (at most 60 type C × 15 min = 15 h), so the constraint is read as 950 minutes.
$$\begin{aligned} \max_{x_A, x_B, x_C}\quad & P = \big(60x_A + 20x_B^2 - 200x_B + 10x_C\big)\times 10^3\\ \text{s.t.}\quad & x_A + x_B + 2x_C = 120 && \text{(labour)}\\ & 10x_A + 5x_B + 15x_C = 950 && \text{(machine)}\\ & 30\,000x_A + 15\,000x_B + 5\,000x_C \le 2.5\times10^6 \iff 6x_A + 3x_B + x_C \le 500 && \text{(budget)}\\ & x_A, x_B, x_C \ge 1 \ \text{(all types made; integers)}. \end{aligned}$$

parts.label: ii
parts.prompt: Write the Lagrangian and the KKT conditions (primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementary slackness).
parts.answer:
Write it as a minimisation of $f = -P/10^3$ (drop the constant scale). With $h_1 = x_A + x_B + 2x_C - 120$, $h_2 = 10x_A + 5x_B + 15x_C - 950$, $g = 6x_A + 3x_B + x_C - 500$:
$$\mathcal L = -(60x_A + 20x_B^2 - 200x_B + 10x_C) + \lambda_1h_1 + \lambda_2h_2 + \mu g.$$
**Stationarity:** $-60 + \lambda_1 + 10\lambda_2 + 6\mu = 0$; $-(40x_B - 200) + \lambda_1 + 5\lambda_2 + 3\mu = 0$; $-10 + 2\lambda_1 + 15\lambda_2 + \mu = 0$.
**Primal feasibility:** $h_1 = 0$, $h_2 = 0$, $g \le 0$. **Dual feasibility:** $\mu \ge 0$ ($\lambda_1, \lambda_2$ free). **Complementary slackness:** $\mu g = 0$.

parts.label: iii
parts.prompt: Use the KKT conditions to find $x_A, x_B, x_C$ that maximise profit (ignore non-negativity).
parts.answer:
**Use the equalities first.** Machine − 10 × labour: $-5x_B - 5x_C = -250 \Rightarrow x_C = 50 - x_B$; then $x_A = 120 - x_B - 2x_C = 20 + x_B$. On this line
$$P/10^3 = 60(20 + x_B) + 20x_B^2 - 200x_B + 10(50 - x_B) = 20x_B^2 - 150x_B + 1700,$$
a **convex** parabola in $x_B$ - so the maximum is at an end of the allowed range, not at the stationary point. Budget: $6(20 + x_B) + 3x_B + (50 - x_B) = 170 + 8x_B \le 500 \Rightarrow x_B \le 41.25$.

**Case μ = 0** (budget slack): stationarity reduces to $\tfrac{d}{dx_B}(-P) = 0 \Rightarrow x_B = 3.75$ (λ₁ = −160, λ₂ = 22). A KKT point - but it is the profit **minimum** (P = 1418.75 × 10³); reject.

**Case μ > 0** (budget active): $x_B = 41.25$, $x_A = 61.25$, $x_C = 8.75$. Stationarity with $40x_B - 200 = 1450$:
$$\lambda_1 + 10\lambda_2 + 6\mu = 60,\quad \lambda_1 + 5\lambda_2 + 3\mu = 1450,\quad 2\lambda_1 + 15\lambda_2 + \mu = 10$$
gives $\lambda_1 = 2840$, $\lambda_2 = -390.5$, $\mu = 187.5 \ge 0$ ✓ - all KKT conditions hold.

**Optimum:** $x_A = 61.25$, $x_B = 41.25$, $x_C = 8.75$, $P = 29\,543.75 \times 10^3$ Rs. As whole PCBs: $x_B = 41$, $x_A = 61$, $x_C = 9$ (budget 498 ≤ 500 ✓), $P = 29\,170 \times 10^3$ Rs.

points.text: Eliminate to x_C = 50 − x_B, x_A = 20 + x_B
Profit as convex quadratic in x_B

parts.label: iv
parts.prompt: If only one type of PCB is made, which type maximises profit?
parts.answer:
With one type, the two equalities cannot both hold (A alone needs 120 labour h but then 1200 machine min ≠ 950), so treat labour, machine and budget as **upper limits**:
- **A only:** $x_A \le 120$ (labour), $\le 95$ (machine), $\le 83.3$ (budget) → 83 units, $P = 60 \times 83 = 4\,980 \times 10^3$.
- **B only:** $x_B \le 120$, $\le 190$, $\le 166.7$ → 120 units, $P = 20 \times 120 \times 110 = 264\,000 \times 10^3$.
- **C only:** $2x_C \le 120 \Rightarrow 60$, $\le 63.3$, $\le 500$ → 60 units, $P = 600 \times 10^3$.

**Type B** - its profit grows quadratically ($20x_B(x_B - 10)$), so it dominates at volume.

points.text: Each type: binding limit and profit

questions.explain: Part (iii) is where most marks go: show the second case. A KKT point is only a candidate - with a convex objective in a maximisation the interior KKT point is the worst choice.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Consider $\min_{\mathbf{x}} f = \tfrac12\mathbf{a}^T\tilde{\mathbf{x}}$ with $\tilde{\mathbf{x}} = [x_1^2, x_2^2, x_3^2]^T$ and $\mathbf{a} = [a_1, a_2, a_3]^T$.
(i) Gradient descent with step size α: write $x_1^{(k+1)}, x_2^{(k+1)}, x_3^{(k+1)}$. **[5]**
(ii) Compute the rate of change $(x_i^{(k+1)} - x_i^{(k)})/x_i^{(k)}$. **[3]**
(iii) With $a_1 = 10^{-4}$, $a_2 = a_3 = 1$ and $\mathbf{x}^{(0)} = [5, 5, 5]^T$, comment on the progress of gradient descent. **[5]**
(iv) Propose two first-order methods that perform better here. **[2]**
parts.answer:
**(i)** $f = \tfrac12(a_1x_1^2 + a_2x_2^2 + a_3x_3^2)$, so $\partial f/\partial x_i = a_ix_i$ and
$$x_i^{(k+1)} = x_i^{(k)} - \alpha a_ix_i^{(k)} = (1 - \alpha a_i)\,x_i^{(k)},\quad i = 1, 2, 3.$$

**(ii)** $\dfrac{x_i^{(k+1)} - x_i^{(k)}}{x_i^{(k)}} = -\alpha a_i$ - each coordinate shrinks geometrically by its own factor $(1 - \alpha a_i)$.

**(iii)** Stability needs $\lvert 1 - \alpha a_i\rvert < 1$ for all $i$, i.e. $\alpha < 2/\max a_i = 2$. With α ≈ 1, $x_2, x_3$ reach 0 almost at once, but $x_1$ only shrinks by a factor $1 - 10^{-4}$ per step: to bring $x_1$ from 5 to $10^{-3}$ needs $k \approx \ln(5/10^{-3})/10^{-4} \approx 85\,000$ iterations. The problem is **ill-conditioned** (condition number $a_{max}/a_{min} = 10^4$): one step size cannot suit both the steep ($x_2, x_3$) and the flat ($x_1$) directions, and choosing α > 2 to speed up $x_1$ makes $x_2, x_3$ diverge. Progress towards the global minimum (0, 0, 0) is extremely slow.

**(iv)** Any two of: **momentum** / **Nesterov momentum** (accumulate speed along the consistently flat $x_1$ direction); **Adagrad**, **RMSProp** or **Adam** (per-coordinate step sizes - divide by the gradient history, so the tiny-gradient $x_1$ gets a large effective step).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Five samples drawn from a multivariate normal are used by the cross-entropy method to **maximise** $f(\mathbf{x}) = 5x_1^2 - x_2^2$:

| i | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $x_{1,i}$ | 4 | 8 | 6 | 10 | 12 |
| $x_{2,i}$ | 5 | 25 | 15 | 10 | 0 |

(i) Which three elite samples are used, and why? **[2]** (ii) Compute the mean vector and covariance matrix for the next iteration. **[8]**
parts.answer:
**(i)** $f$ values: 55, −305, −45, 400, 720. For maximisation the elites are the three **largest**: samples **5 (720), 4 (400) and 1 (55)**.

**(ii)** Maximum-likelihood refit on the elites $\{(12, 0), (10, 10), (4, 5)\}$:
$$\boldsymbol\mu = \tfrac13\big[(12 + 10 + 4),\ (0 + 10 + 5)\big] = [8.667,\ 5]^T.$$
Deviations $\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol\mu$: (3.333, −5), (1.333, 5), (−4.667, 0).
$$\Sigma = \frac13\sum(\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol\mu)(\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol\mu)^T = \frac13\begin{bmatrix}11.11 + 1.78 + 21.78 & -16.67 + 6.67 + 0\\ \cdot & 25 + 25 + 0\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}11.56 & -3.33\\ -3.33 & 16.67\end{bmatrix}.$$
(Dividing by $m - 1 = 2$ instead - the unbiased estimate - gives [[17.33, −5], [−5, 25]]; the course's ML refit uses $1/m$.)

questions.explain: For CE always check the direction: these notes minimise by default, but this question maximises - pick the largest f.
